lines.say: Would you rather take a training like this?
In the first one, you learn by playing: you see your progress, you get feedback, and you stay motivated.
In this one, people only see an obligation. They stop paying attention, and the quality of learning drops.
Get one wrong, and you see why right away. That's the moment people actually learn.
And the best part? Gamification improves learning and motivation, and reduces dropout.
You don't need a new course. Take the quiz you already have, and add three things.
So, how do you want your training to feel?

caption:
Would you rather take a training like this, or like this? Comment TRAINING and we'll send you our free guide.

Same cybersecurity training, same questions. One is a form: answer, click Next, no idea if you got it right. The other is a game: lives, a countdown that sets your points, a progress bar and instant feedback on every answer.

You don't need a new course. Take the quiz you already have and add 3 things:

1. A timer: answer faster, score more.
2. Lives: mistakes cost something, but never end the game.
3. Instant feedback: get one wrong and see why right away.

That's gamification in employee training.

Source: Sailer & Homner (2020), "The Gamification of Learning: a Meta-analysis", Educational Psychology Review 32, 77-112.
